words.defn_en: to gather separate things into a whole; a total or collection formed in this way:
words.defn_zh: 匯集；聚集；總計；集合體；總體的
words.root_note: ad- or ag- (to or toward) + greg (flock or herd)

sentences.en: The analytics website can ______ millions of user reviews into one easy-to-read rating.
sentences.zh: 數據分析網站可以匯集數百萬則使用者評論，形成一個容易閱讀的評分。

sentences.en: Although each donation was small, its ______ value provided the campaign with ten million dollars.
sentences.zh: 儘管單筆捐款很小，但其總計價值為競選活動提供了一千萬美元。

words.defn_en: fond of company and social activity, or naturally living together in groups:
words.defn_zh: 合群的；愛交際的；群居的
words.root_note: greg (flock or herd) + -ious (full of or having the quality of)

sentences.en: Wolves are highly ______ animals that depend on complex pack structures to hunt and protect their territory.
sentences.zh: 狼是高度群居的動物，依賴複雜的群體結構捕獵並保護領地。

sentences.en: Known for his ______ nature, the diplomat introduced himself to dozens of dignitaries at the gala.
sentences.zh: 這位外交官以愛交際的性格聞名，在晚宴上主動認識數十位外國政要。

words.defn_en: outstandingly and shockingly bad, wrong, or offensive:
words.defn_zh: 極其惡劣的；令人震驚的；明目張膽的
words.root_note: e- or ex- (out of) + greg (flock); literally, standing out from the flock

sentences.en: The audit exposed an ______ accounting error that cost the corporation millions of dollars.
sentences.zh: 審計揭露一項極其惡劣的會計錯誤，使公司損失數百萬美元。

sentences.en: The judge's refusal to admit vital DNA evidence was an ______ violation of constitutional rights.
sentences.zh: 法官拒絕採納關鍵 DNA 證據，是對憲法權利極其惡劣的侵犯。

words.defn_en: to gather together in a crowd or group:

sentences.en: Thousands of fans began to ______ outside the stadium before the championship match.
sentences.zh: 冠軍賽前，數千名球迷開始在體育場外聚集。

sentences.en: Hundreds of manatees ______ in warm coastal waters during the winter mating season.
sentences.zh: 冬季交配季節，數百頭海牛會聚集在溫暖的沿海水域。

words.defn_en: to separate a person or group from others, often according to a particular characteristic:
words.defn_zh: 隔離；分開；實施種族隔離
words.root_note: se- (apart or away) + greg (flock or herd) + -ate (act)

sentences.en: Technicians had to ______ infected plant tissue from healthy control samples.
sentences.zh: 技術人員必須將受感染的植物組織與健康對照樣本隔離。

sentences.en: The museum documents laws once used to ______ citizens by race in schools and public transportation.
sentences.zh: 博物館記錄過去用來在學校與公共交通中按種族隔離公民的法律。

words.defn_en: to end an official policy that separates people according to race:
words.defn_zh: 廢除種族隔離；取消隔離政策

sentences.en: The Supreme Court ruling forced school boards to ______ public classrooms.
sentences.zh: 最高法院裁決迫使學校董事會立即廢除公立教室的種族隔離。

sentences.en: Civil-rights leaders organized boycotts to pressure stores to ______ their lunch counters.
sentences.zh: 民權領袖組織抵制活動，施壓商店取消午餐櫃檯的隔離政策。

words.defn_en: a dense crowd of people or animals; to crowd into or fill a place:
words.root_note: Germanic origin meaning to press or crowd closely together

sentences.en: An eager ______ of fans and photographers surged forward when the singer left the hotel.
sentences.zh: 歌手離開飯店時，一大群熱切的粉絲和攝影記者蜂擁上前。

sentences.en: Every December, tourists ______ the historic squares to see the holiday lights and winter markets.
sentences.zh: 每年十二月，遊客會擠滿歷史廣場，欣賞節日燈飾和冬季市集。

words.defn_en: to collect a large quantity of money, information, objects, or power over time:
words.root_note: ad- (to or toward) + massa (mass or large quantity)

sentences.en: By investing early in software startups, the venture capitalist managed to ______ a vast fortune.
sentences.zh: 這位創投家透過早期投資軟體新創公司，成功累積巨額財富。

sentences.en: Journalists worked with whistleblowers to ______ documents proving corporate tax evasion.
sentences.zh: 記者與吹哨者合作，收集證明企業逃稅的文件。

words.defn_en: to come together and form one larger group, mass, or whole:

sentences.en: Residents began to ______ into an organized coalition when the city threatened to demolish the park.
sentences.zh: 市政府威脅拆除公園後，居民開始凝聚成有組織的聯盟。

sentences.en: Gravity causes cosmic dust particles to slowly ______ and eventually form new planets.
sentences.zh: 引力使宇宙塵埃顆粒緩慢匯聚，最終形成新的行星。

words.defn_en: a group of animals of one kind, or a large group of people; to move them together in a controlled direction:
words.defn_zh: 獸群；人群；成群驅趕；引導
words.root_note: Germanic origin referring to animals kept together

sentences.en: Security guards had to ______ the crowd through narrow side doors during the fire drill.
sentences.zh: 消防演習時，保全必須引導人群通過狹窄的側門。

sentences.en: Economists study how ______ mentality encourages investors to imitate the broader crowd.
sentences.zh: 經濟學家研究羊群心理如何促使投資者模仿大眾。

words.defn_en: a collection of separate texts, facts, recordings, or other materials gathered into one work:
words.root_note: con- (together) + pilare (gather or heap up) + -ion (act or result)

sentences.en: The professor published a thick ______ of nineteenth-century feminist essays.
sentences.zh: 教授出版了一本厚厚的十九世紀女性主義散文彙編。

sentences.en: The firm released a comprehensive ______ of cybersecurity rules from several departments.
sentences.zh: 公司發布一份彙集各部門規則的完整網路安全協定合集。

words.defn_en: to assemble people for inspection or action, or to gather enough strength, courage, or support:
words.defn_zh: 召集；集合；鼓起；聚集力量
words.root_note: Latin monstrare (to show or put on display)

sentences.en: The general ordered his officers to ______ all available troops in the central courtyard.
sentences.zh: 將軍命令軍官在中央庭院召集所有可用部隊。

sentences.en: Despite severe stage fright, the cellist managed to ______ enough courage to perform.
sentences.zh: 儘管非常怯場，這位大提琴家仍鼓起足夠勇氣上台演出。
